name: headache overview
title: A headache is screened for SNOOP4 red flags to rule out a secondary cause (subarachnoid hemorrhage, bacterial meningitis, giant cell arteritis, brain tumour, idiopathic intracranial hypertension, each with its first test and treatment) from a list of causes by category, while the primary headache is named by its ICHD-3 features (migraine, tension-type, cluster) and treated acutely (with the triptan and NSAID contraindications) and preventively, watching for medication overuse headache

root.title: Headache: rule OUT a secondary cause while you name the primary one
lines: history of the pain: NILDOCAAFIAT · Nature, Intensity, Location, Duration, Onset, Contributing, Aggravating, Alleviating, Frequency, Impact, Attribute, Treatment tried

SNOOP4 red flags: Systemic (fever, weight loss) · Neurological deficits · Older onset (over 50) · Onset sudden (thunderclap) · Papilledema · Positional · Precipitated by Valsalva · Progressive or a new pattern
positional: worse LYING → raised pressure, mass · worse UPRIGHT → intracranial HYPOTENSION
examine: vital signs · fundi (papilledema) · pupils, eye movements, visual fields · neurological exam · body habitus · neck · scalp · jaw joint

groups.title: PRIMARY: no red flag
lines: name it by its International Classification of Headache Disorders (ICHD-3) features

pres.title: Secondary causes to EXCLUDE
lines: • vascular: stroke, ICH, SAH, venous thrombosis, PRES, RCVS, dissection, vasculitis
• inflammatory: giant cell arteritis, idiopathic intracranial hypertension
• trauma: after dural puncture, concussion · drugs: medication overuse
• tumour: meningioma, schwannoma, pituitary apoplexy, choriocarcinoma

pres.title: Beware MEDICATION OVERUSE headache
lines: • triptans 10+ days, simple analgesics 15+ days a month, for over 3 months
• → 15+ headache days a month in a primary headache

head: h
Subarachnoid hemorrhage
aneurysm
clue: case: 52 y lifting groceries · BP 185/100 · stiff neck, alert, no focal signs
inv: • sensitivity 98% day 0 · 76% day 2 · 50% at 1 week · 30% at 2 weeks
tx: untreated, it re-bleeds: 15% in 24 h, 40% in a month

head: h
Bacterial meningitis
clue: • Kernig: knee extension hurts neck or back
• Brudzinski: neck flexion flexes hips + knees
case: 21 y student, 1 day · T 39.4, HR 124 · drowsy, 1-step commands
inv: image first if signs of raised pressure
tx: • never wait for imaging or LP

head: h
Giant cell arteritis
over 50
clue: case: 74 y, 2 weeks left temporal · hurts to brush hair, chewing · 2 episodes transient left vision loss · tender thick temporal artery
tx: don't wait for the biopsy · untreated → permanent vision loss · then taper

head: h
Brain tumour
a mass, raised pressure
clue: case: 58 y, 2 months · forgetful, first seizure · left pronator drift, BOTH discs swollen
inv: • (CT if no MRI) · papilledema = raised pressure
• CT chest, abdomen, pelvis: primary or secondary?

head: h
Idiopathic intracranial hypertension
obesity · steroids · vitamin A · tetracycline
clue: case: 27 y, BMI 37, gained 15 kg · 6 weeks daily headache · papilledema, acuity normal
inv: • excludes a mass or venous sinus thrombosis
• MRI: empty sella, flat back of globe, venous sinus stenosis
• then LP: opening pressure over 250 mm H2O
tx: • topiramate · shunt, optic nerve sheath fenestration

head: h
Migraine
prodrome (2-48 h) · aura (25-30%, 5-60 min) · headache · postdrome (24-48 h)
trigeminovascular · CGRP release
3rd most prevalent, 7th most disabling
clue: • aura: spreading, fully reversible · visual (zigzags), sensory, language
case: 4 h + photophobia + nausea → migraine, not tension
inv: 5 attacks · 4-72 h (4 hours to 3 days) · 2 of 4 features · 1 of nausea or light + sound
tx: PREVENT if over 4 a month or disabling
• or acute drugs fail, not tolerated, overuse risk
• SEEDS: Sleep, Exercise, Eat, Diary, Stress

head: h
Tension-type
the most prevalent (38% a year)
inv: at most one of light or sound sensitivity

head: h
Cluster
0.1% · men 3:1 · ~30 · 85% smokers · alcohol
lasts ~15 years · "suicide headache"
clue: STRICTLY one side, at the eye
• severe · 15-180 min · every other day to 8 a day
• same-side tearing, red eye, runny nose, ptosis
• RESTLESS, paces (migraine lies still) · same time of day or year
inv: the hypothalamus drives it → circadian, circannual rhythm
